description.narrative: The objectives of the Project are to improve the outcomes of the CCT Program, including the CCT Program response to COVID-19, and to strengthen the integration of the social protection system for the extreme poor and the vulnerable.

The objectives of the Social Protection Integration Project are to improve the outcomes of the urban component of the CCT Program and to strengthen the integration of the social protection system for the extreme poor. There are four components to the project, the first component being strengthening of the urban conditional cash transfer program and implementation of the integrated transition strategy. This component will finance cash transfers for the reformed urban CCT Program and the design and implementation of the urban transition strategy in the three pilot municipalities. This component includes two subcomponents: urban CCT program reform and financing of cash transfers, and first phase implementation of the urban transition strategy. The second component is the institutional strengthening for the CCT Program and Integration of the social protection system. This component includes two subcomponents: reinforcement of the CCT program delivery system, and institutional strengthening for the integration of the social protection system. The third component is the project management. This component will support the UCP by financing key staff including: one project technical specialist, one dedicated procurement specialist; two procurement assistants; one financial management; one disbursement specialist; one accountant; and one monitoring specialist. The project will finance the operational cost for the management and planning of the project activities, as well as the external audit for the project. Finally, the fourth component is the contingency emergency response. Reflecting the strategic approach taken in Honduras across the World Bank's portfolio, this component will finance immediate response to eligible emergencies. As such, in the event of such an eligible emergency, this component would finance emergency activities and expenditures through the reallocation of funds from the project that meet conditions detailed in the financing agreement and project operations manual for the project.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries of social safety net programs

comment.narrative: In 2022 and 2023, an exception was introduced in response to a climate emergency, allowing all rural households in targeted municipalities registered in SIRBHO to receive cash transfers. However, in 2024, this exception was not extended, and the cash transfers reverted to being paid only to those households selected by the current targeting method in SIRBHO. At the same time, new households were incorporated into the program. This ISR reflects the 258, 289 households receiving benefits form the CCT program and paid by Dec 2024. The cash transfer program is also set to expand to urban areas in 2025 but payments in 2025 have not taken place yet. The estimation of beneficiaries is Number of rural households enrolled in the CT program * 4.63 persons per household + Number of urban households enrolled in the CT program * 4.08 persons per household.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries of social safety net programs

comment.narrative: Partially achieved. Cumulative unique beneficiaries over the project period totaled 3.2 million of individuals. To avoid double counting, these individuals were calculated counting the number of individuals once if they were CCT beneficiaries at least once in the lifetime of the project. However, the indicator is reported annually, not cumulatively, as per project M&E arrangements. Annual coverages were not fully achieved in all years but coverage of around 1.2million individuals was maintained during the implementation period. The indicator is calculated by adding rural households × 4.63 and urban households × 4.08. While coverage was nearly on target (99%) in 2020–2021, it declined from 2022, primarily due to reduced IDB funding and a strategic shift in program targeting and redesign. By October 2025, the program preliminary planned to reach 922,832 beneficiaries (205,031 households). The compliance verification report expected in March 2026 will provide the final numbers for the ICR

title.narrative: 6. Unification of the urban and rural CCTs for the integration of the CCT Program

baseline.value: Urban and Rural CCTs operated separately

comment.narrative: Achieved. This indicator was originally classified as an intermediate indicator but was elevated to the Project Development Objective (PDO) level with the 2024 restructuring. The program was unified under a single operational manual beginning in 2019, representing a milestone in standardizing procedures and integrating both components for consistent implementation. It continued to function as a single program even after the program reform in 2022.

title.narrative: 4. School retention from 9th to 10th grade for children of CCT beneficiary households in rural areas

comment.narrative: The indicator is calculated using 2024 enrollment rates in education and reported annually. However, no education cash transfers were provided during 2024, meaning families did not receive financial support for improving their children's education outcomes. As a result, the indicator is not expected to increase. Additionally, the education data is currently incomplete/preliminary, as some isolated municipalities report their statistics later in the new year. Consequently, the indicator may improve once additional data becomes available in the coming months when the PRS provides the official report for year 2025.

title.narrative: 4. School retention from 9th to 10th grade for children of CCT beneficiary households in rural areas

comment.narrative: Achieved. Although this indicator was recalculated to ensure consistency and the use of the latest education administrative databases for this last ISR, it did not have the initial calculation problems as the previous indicator. This indicator, introduced in the 2024 restructuring, enables precise measurement of the program's contribution at one of the most vulnerable stages of the educational trajectory. The recalculations show a progressive improvement in retention rates, rising from 44% in 2023 to 47.5% in 2024 and reaching 50.2% in 2025. These annual values not only surpass the established targets for each year but also demonstrate a sustained upward trend.

title.narrative: 1. Rural CCT beneficiaries who are in the bottom two quintiles of the income distribution

comment.narrative: Achieved. Due to data limitations, a new source of data, SIRBHO, is being used to have an approximation for the value of the indicator under a set of assumptions. To calculate this value in 2025 the EPHPM 2023 was used in combination of the SIRBHO and SIRES databases.

title.narrative: 1. Rural CCT beneficiaries who are in the bottom two quintiles of the income distribution

comment.narrative: Achieved. This indicator, recalculated to address reporting challenges in past ISRs along with measurement challenges following the program's reform, consistently exceeded its annual target. From 2020 to 2022, it rose from 55.3% to 72.5%, reflecting improved targeting of rural beneficiaries in the lowest income quintiles. Despite temporary inclusion of non-poor households in 2023 due to emergency measures, by 2024 the share remained strong at 65.1%, confirming enhanced targeting efficiency. By project close, three out of four rural beneficiaries (73.10 %) belonged to the bottom two income quintiles, demonstrating sustained improvements in beneficiary selection.

title.narrative: 3. School retention from 6th to 7th grade for children of CCT beneficiary households in rural areas

comment.narrative: Not achieved. The indicator was introduced in the 2024 restructuring. It was recalculated in 2025 to resolve persistent data quality issues, including inconsistent education databases and misaligned grade levels in the original baseline and targets and ISR reported values. The baseline and targets for this indicator were not accurately calculated because the education databases available during the last project restructuring were inconsistent and lacked proper data dictionaries. As a result, the values used reflected third grade retention rather than the intended sixth grade, leading to misaligned targets and baseline figures. While the revised analysis shows stable retention rates of 44–45% throughout the project 2022-2025—even amid major external shocks—targets were not met due to flaws in the restructuring target-setting process.
